clue.text: A couple of staff writers canned

definitions.meaning: two composers of the Romantic era, people who wrote notes on the musical staff (stave)
canned is slang for drunk; the pair of composers is Cockney rhyming slang for 'pissed'

explanation.surface: Two office scribes have just been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees and 'canned' suggests fired; in fact staff is the five-line musical stave and canned means drunk, via Cockney rhyming slang (two composers' names rhyme with 'pissed').
explanation.definitionFit: Two famous nineteenth-century composers, and also rhyming slang for intoxicated, which canned means in British slang.

clue.text: Complicated procedure to achieve propagation

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tricky medical or laboratory method is needed for breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed or multiply offspring is to bring about propagation, a direct synonym relation.

clue.text: Monumental but not grand appearance

indicators.note: but not says one piece is left out of the word before it

parts.note: monumental means huge
G is the common abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A statue that looks impressive, yet not quite grand.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint or shade gives something its look, so colour stands for outward appearance.

clue.text: Attach with molten alloy, keeping current plug away

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to fix one metal part to another with melted tin-lead alloy is to solder it on
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: Instructions for an electrician joining wires with solder while the power stays off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks electrical in the soldering picture but simply supplies I.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep working doggedly despite difficulty is to persevere, the idiomatic sense of plugging away.

clue.text: Racket involving island barricade set up for migrant

indicators.note: in a down answer, set up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
involving means taking in, so one piece wraps around the others

parts.note: a racket is a con, a swindle
a dam is a barrier, a barricade across water

explanation.surface: A scam involving an island barricade put up to stop incoming migrants.
explanation.definitionFit: Migrant as an adjective describes animals or people that wander from place to place, which is the wandering sense here.

clue.text: Air bags suspended, keeping the head well down

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, is moved well down to the bottom of this down answer

parts.note: suspended means hung up, slung

explanation.surface: Advice to someone hanging in a harness: keep your head low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping the head well down' sends the S of SLUNG to the foot of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The paired organs of breathing fill and empty with air, so they are fairly described as bags for air.

clue.text: Old Nick's peculiar behaviour

parts.note: peculiar means strange
ways means habits, behaviour

explanation.surface: The Devil (Old Nick) has odd habits.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Nick is usually the Devil; here nick is British slang for prison. Strangeways is the old name of the Manchester jail, now HMP Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manchester prison carried this name for over a century before renaming, so it is literally an old jail.

clue.text: Breed cow's stomach with an extra loop near the bottom

indicators.text: with an extra loop near the bottom
indicators.note: drawing a second loop at the foot of a letter P turns it into a B

parts.note: tripe is the stomach lining of a cow, eaten as food

explanation.surface: A recipe note for tripe, adding a loop of something at the base.
explanation.walkthrough: A visual trick: add a lower bowl to the letter P and it becomes B.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed is a group of related stock sharing descent, which is a family group or clan.

clue.text: Source of electric shock holds interest

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to appal is to shock or horrify

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An electric shock's origin grabs attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Attraction or allure is what something has when it draws interest, a near synonym.

clue.text: Second person being dishonest about reversing train

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second

indicators.note: reversing tells us to read the pieces just before it backwards

parts.note: a liar is someone being dishonest
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone else lying about a train going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-track rail vehicle is a type of railway carriage set, so it is an example of a train.

clue.text: Canoodler suggesting the last five of 10?

indicators.note: the final five letters of the named entry are what the answer's two words describe

parts.note: 10 across, whose final five letters are O then RAIL: O stands for love (nil in tennis) and a rail is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A cuddler hinting at the end of a train's name.
explanation.walkthrough: The final five letters of 10 across are O and RAIL: O is love (zero in tennis) and a rail is a wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Canoodling is kissing and cuddling, and a romantically doting partner is called this affectionate pet name.

clue.text: Tied sporting contests repeated, ignoring first time and promoting the next

indicators.note: ignoring the first one means the first of the two such letters is dropped
promoting the next means the following such letter moves up earlier in the word
repeated means the word is written twice

parts.note: events are sporting contests

explanation.surface: Drawn matches being replayed, with a scheduling shuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: EVENTSEVENTS loses its first T to give EVENSEVENTS; 'promoting the next' moves the remaining T up to the start of the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: When two sides finish level, with the score all square, the informal phrase for that equal result is used.

clue.text: Taken to court to seize billion, getting back tanner

indicators.note: to seize means to grab and hold, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sued means taken to court

indicators.note: getting back means the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: bn is the usual abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: Someone sued to recover a billion and getting money back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanner' looks like an old British sixpence; here it is a device that tans the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanning couch with ultraviolet lamps browns the skin, so it is literally something that tans.

clue.text: Oddly absent, if mummies are angry

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters go missing, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Mummies get cross if someone is missing for strange reasons.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe with anger is to be angry, a direct verbal synonym.

clue.text: Did glance twist a smidgen when speaking?

indicators.note: when speaking means the words are to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: to twist is to rick (wrench a joint) and a smidgen is a shade, a tiny amount

explanation.surface: Did someone just shoot a quick look, twisting slightly, while talking?
explanation.walkthrough: Rick a shade, said quickly, gives the rebounding verb. 'Glance' here means to bounce off at an angle, not to look.
explanation.definitionFit: A projectile that glances off a surface bounces away at an angle, which is what a rebounding bullet did.

clue.text: Pierced by dagger in odd places, selectively slain or whacked

indicators.note: pierced by means another piece is stuck inside

parts.note: culled means killed off selectively, as with herds

indicators.note: taking the letters in odd places, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A grisly murder report: stabbed, selectively killed or beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone with a heavy club is to whack them, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: A nice dhal could be a spicy dish

indicators.note: could be says these letters might become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasant lentil curry might count as a spicy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' marks A NICE DHAL as letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican rolled tortilla with chilli sauce is an example of a hot, spicy meal.

clue.text: Message perhaps seeking romance for each boy, for each boy

parts.note: per means for each
a son is a boy
a means for each, as in ten pounds a head
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A lonely-hearts note for every single boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase is read two ways: once as PER SON, once as A LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A lonely-hearts notice in a newspaper is a short message placed in hopes of finding a partner.

clue.text: Spill mistakenly around limits of earshot

definitions.text: Spill mistakenly around limits of earshot

indicators.note: around means placed about another piece
mistakenly means wrongly, so the letters are jumbled
the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Blurting out a secret by accident while someone can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a secret spilt by mistake within someone's hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal a secret by accident within someone's hearing is to blurt it, which is the phrasal verb's meaning.

clue.text: Polo maybe having start kicked off with a bow for players

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.note: Marco Polo, the Venetian traveller, is one person called Polo

explanation.surface: A polo match begins with a kick-off and then players bow.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo is the explorer, not the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian direction in sheet music tells string players to use the bow again rather than pluck.

clue.text: First-class return of traveller aboard public transport

indicators.note: return means the letters come back in reverse order
aboard means on board, inside the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is public transport
a rep is a sales representative, a commercial traveller

explanation.surface: A salesman rides the bus home in first class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' reads BREPUS backwards; a commercial traveller is an old term for a salesperson.
explanation.definitionFit: Something excellent or top-quality is first-rate, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Range of Banksy works, for example, defaced

indicators.note: defaced means losing the face, the first letter

parts.note: Banksy, the street artist, paints murals on walls

explanation.surface: A series of Banksy paintings has been vandalised.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian mountain chain dividing Europe from Asia is a range of peaks.

clue.text: Half-forgotten retired South African bishop supporting veto of local languages

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting below the other piece

parts.note: to ban is to veto

indicators.note: half the word is forgotten, keeping only the first half

parts.note: Desmond Tutu was the retired Anglican archbishop of Cape Town

explanation.surface: A retired South African churchman backing a ban on local tongues.
explanation.definitionFit: This family of related tongues is spoken across central and southern Africa, so they are local languages there.

clue.text: Believing jerk gets round hold-up

indicators.note: gets round means wraps around another piece

parts.note: a tic is a nervous jerk
a heist is a robbery, a hold-up

explanation.surface: A nervous twitch spreads during a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding faith in a god is the relation here: someone with religious belief takes this adjective.

clue.text: Protective cloth securing end of divan in one's place

indicators.note: in one's place means the new letter stands where the letter for one was

parts.note: material is cloth

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A fabric cover for the divan, protecting it at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' just joins: N goes in where I (one) stood.
explanation.definitionFit: Motherly feelings are shielding and guarding by instinct, so the adjective implies protectiveness.

clue.text: Power of some base to preserve deadlock

parts.note: a logarithm is the power to which a base is raised; LOG is its short form
jam is a fruit preserve

explanation.surface: A military base's authority used to keep a stalemate in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power' and 'base' sound military but are maths: a logarithm is an exponent of a base.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam of floating timber blocks a river; figuratively the term means a stalemate or impasse.

clue.text: Set side for cricket over

indicators.note: over means turned over, read the other way

parts.note: the leg side (or on side) is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team is chosen for the next over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs; 'over' looks like cricket too.
explanation.definitionFit: When jelly sets it stiffens, and to solidify in that way is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Understand surrealist article containing small joke expressed cumbersomely

indicators.note: containing means holding another piece within

parts.note: to see is to understand
a quip is a joke
Salvador Dali was a surrealist painter
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Getting a surrealist's article with a little joke said in a clunky way.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-winded wording using very long polysyllabic words is the heavy, unwieldy style meant by cumbersome expression.
